_doc: Upgrade recommendations that were considered and REFUSED. The queue is regenerated from agent verdict files every rebuild, so a rejection that lives only in the record is undone on the next cycle — 杏もん堂 was reverted, linted clean, and silently re-promoted three times before this file existed. Approvals persist as safety.owner_signoff; refusals persist here. scripts/apply-gate-tranche.mjs skips every id+field listed.

rejections.name: 杏もん堂 (Almondou)
rejections.by: Claude, on Greg's standing instruction to resolve existence and evidence problems directly
rejections.reason: The recommendation rested on a claim that the shop's own site states the curry uses no wheat flour and passed a third-party gluten/gliadin test with NONE DETECTED, the report displayed in store. almond-cafe.jp was fetched on 2026-08-23: no グルテン, no 小麦不使用, no グリアジン検査, no allergen page of any kind. The shop sells almond butter toast on wheat bread, a spiced curry roux, and cake. The claim is not supported anywhere on the cited source. The record's own detail text was the accurate one.
rejections.note: The same finding also corrected the record's spice count from 18 to 21, which the site does confirm. That correction was kept. A partly-checkable finding is not a trustworthy one.

rejections.name: Osteria Lauro
rejections.reason: Queued only for a paperwork reason — the record had been held down because no safety finding cited a source. The sources still do not hold: BOTH of its GF claims failed verification, the +150 yen gluten-free pasta substitution AND the warning that lunch sets come with bread from a shared kitchen. Nothing here is established in either direction, so the honest tier is "ask". Revisit if a first-party source for the substitution turns up.

rejections.name: そらのいろ ニッポン
rejections.reason: The upgrade rests on a single claim — that staff ask about wheat allergy and cook the order in a separate pot — and that is exactly the claim that failed verification against its cited source. A separate-pot claim is the whole of the safety case at a ramen shop, where the default is shared boiling water, so it needs a real first-party source before it moves.
